question: A user asks Claude to generate a 40-line Python script that parses log files, then five minutes later asks Claude to fix a bug in that same script. Where does the updated script most likely appear so the user can compare it to the earlier version?
options: A) In the artifact panel, updated as a new version accessible through the version selector
B) In a newly created Project, since bug fixes always require project-level knowledge storage
C) Nowhere retrievable, since Claude cannot revise previously generated code in the same conversation
D) In research mode results, since fixing a bug counts as an investigative web search task
correct_answers: A) In the artifact panel, updated as a new version accessible through the version selector
explanations: Correct. A 40-line script is substantial, self-contained content suited to an artifact; when Claude revises it, the update appears in the same artifact panel, and the version selector lets the user switch between the original and fixed versions.
Fixing a bug in an already-generated script does not require creating a new Project; the existing artifact already supports iterative revision without added project structure.
Claude can revise previously generated code within the same conversation, and with an artifact, the fixed version remains retrievable through version history.
Research mode is for gathering external information via web search, not for revising code that Claude already generated in the conversation.
